features.text: Gabriel is a 43-year-old male.
Gabriel has a past medical history of diabetes, high blood pressure, and high cholesterol.
Gabriel experienced back pain that started four days ago after bending over to pick something up in the yard.
The back pain radiates down Gabriel's left leg.
Gabriel experiences pain in his lower back and left leg, with some tingling in certain positions.
Gabriel has not experienced any weakness, numbness, loss of bowel or bladder function.
Gabriel has not had any back surgeries but has had occasional back pain in the past.
Gabriel has tried ibuprofen for the pain, which helped some.
Gabriel's HbA1c was 7.1 in the past, and he checks his blood sugar two to three times a week, usually in the 120-140 range.
Gabriel is on Norvasc 5 mg once daily for high blood pressure.
Gabriel checks his blood pressure once a week or every few weeks, usually in the 120-130/70-80 range.
Gabriel has experienced ankle swelling, which started a month or two after starting Norvasc.
Gabriel's physical exam shows tenderness in the left paraspinal area of the lower back.
Gabriel has a 2/6 systolic ejection murmur, which is not new.
Gabriel has 1+ non-pitting edema in the lower extremities.
Gabriel has no signs of deep vein thrombosis (negative Homans sign, no calf tenderness).
Gabriel's neurological exam is normal, and his straight leg raise test is negative.
Gabriel has a history of diabetes and is trying to control his diet, though he still eats cookies.
Gabriel is aware of the importance of diet and exercise for managing diabetes.
Gabriel has a history of occasional back pain but no prior surgeries.
